when: 2026-08-02, on origin/main before any edit of this branch
what: The size of the post-combat clinch, named as a quantity and taken on the seed matrix. Nobody had measured what the owner's sentence corresponds to, so this file defines the measurement first and reports it second.
theOwnersWords: Когда все сгрудились после боя — потом не могут некоторое время разойтись и блокируют друг друга.

tree.note: The base commit is on `main` and survives squash; the branch head is not, so it is described in prose instead (Issue #106). No file of the simulation is changed by this branch at the point these numbers were taken — only the test project gained the harness below.

howItWasMeasured.harness: tests/DungeonFortress.Simulation.Tests/PrototypePostCombatDispersalTests.cs, added by this branch. It walks each party tick by tick with PrototypeWorld.Step() and reads PrototypeWorld.GetSnapshot() after every tick.
howItWasMeasured.refusedSteps: Read from the canonical event log by LastTick, the way PrototypeTrafficTests reads them. A repeated identical decision coalesces into one entry whose LastTick advances on every tick it repeats, so scanning for LastTick == acted sees it on each of those ticks. Positions, modes and LastMoveTick are read from the snapshot, which does not coalesce.

definitions.cohort: the creatures in CreatureMode.Fighting on the tick before the wave's EndTick — exactly the set ResolveWave turns back into Waiting on that tick
definitions.window: the 60 ticks after EndTick. Sixty because the dungeon is 28 tiles wide, a harvest is 12 ticks and a cook batch 24, and it is a sixth of T.wave_interval_ticks, so it never reaches the next fight
definitions.measuredWindow: a window with at least one tick in it. Three of the sixteen waves end on the same tick the party does; they are printed and left out of every aggregate
definitions.clinchTicks: ticks of the window on which at least two cohort members were refused a step (waiting_blocked_by_other). Two, because one creature waiting for one tile is ordinary traffic
definitions.maxBlockedTogether: the most cohort members refused a step on one tick of one window
definitions.blocked: cohort creature-ticks with a refused step inside the window
definitions.background: the same counts over the 60 ticks immediately before that wave arrived, for the same creatures. This is the peacetime control
definitions.dispersalDelay: per cohort member, ticks from EndTick to the first tick it stands somewhere else; 60 if it never does
definitions.standingStill: cohort creature-ticks that neither moved nor were refused a step
definitions.idleAndStill: standingStill restricted to CreatureMode.Waiting — standing with no work rather than standing to do work
definitions.shortDetour: refused steps where a route to the same destination existed within 4 extra steps once every other creature counted as a wall
definitions.walledIn: refused steps where no such route existed at all
definitions.nextTileFree: refused steps where the tile the step was for was empty at the end of the tick — the step was refused by the arbitration, not by a body
definitions.byArrived: refused steps whose next tile was held by a creature standing on its own destination. PrototypeWorld.CanYield refuses to order such a creature aside, so no yield can ever clear these
definitions.byUrgent: next tile held by a creature with a meal reserved or mustering — CanYield refuses these too unless the block is a proven dependency cycle
definitions.byEligible: next tile held by a creature CanYield would allow to step aside

whereItHappens.reading: (10,7) and (11,7) are the kitchen, (14,7) and (15,7) the larder — the two doorways of the room the raiders walk to. (24,12) and (22,12) are the corridor of the south-eastern chamber the gate opens onto.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: The post-combat window is not, on the matrix as a whole, more blocked than peacetime.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: clinchTicks 154 against 194 in the control (ratio 0.79) and 782 refused steps against 737 (ratio 1.06), over 13 measured windows and 3780 cohort creature-ticks.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: The clinch is not a state the end of a fight creates. It is the dungeon's ordinary traffic, into which the end of a fight drops six to nine creatures at the same doorway at the same moment.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: It is nevertheless real, and its size is a single window rather than an average.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: baseline/20260727 wave 1: 292 refused steps in 60 ticks by a cohort of nine — 54 % of that cohort's creature-ticks — against 81 in the control window of the same nine creatures, a ratio of 3.6. Six of the nine were refused a step on the same tick. clinchTicks 53 of 60.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: This is the party the owner would have been watching. On the same matrix prepared/20260726 wave 1 goes the other way — 68 refused against 156 in its own control — so the corridor is a property of the run and not of the design (13.4).

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: The larger half of «не могут разойтись» is not blocking at all.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: 1989 of 3780 cohort creature-ticks (53 %) were spent neither moving nor being refused a step, and 1121 of them (30 % of the window) in CreatureMode.Waiting. The commonest last decision of such a creature is waiting_stock_sufficient, 850 times: there is no work to be had. On baseline/20260728 wave 1 seven of eight ex-combatants never left the tile the fight ended on in 60 ticks, with 0 refused steps in the whole window.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: Two different pictures produce one complaint. A group that stands because it is jammed and a group that stands because the larder is full look the same from above, and the second is the bigger of the two.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: Of the refused steps, almost all had a way round.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: 728 of 782 (93.1 %) had a route to the same destination within 4 extra steps once every other creature was treated as a wall. Only 24 (3.1 %) had no route at all.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: The creature is not walled in. PrototypeMap.NextStep is a BFS that does not see bodies, so it hands out a step that Move then refuses, and the tile to walk around by is standing empty.

whatTheNumbersSay.claim: The yield arbitration cannot clear most of these even in principle.
whatTheNumbersSay.evidence: 307 of 782 refused steps (39 %) were blocked by a creature standing on its own destination, which PrototypeWorld.CanYield refuses to order aside; 54 more by a creature with a meal reserved or mustering, which it also refuses. On 680 of 782 (87 %) no chosen_traffic_yield was planned anywhere in the world on that tick.
whatTheNumbersSay.reading: 328 refused steps were blocked by somebody who could have been asked to move, so the arbitration is not powerless — but the largest single class is one it is designed never to touch.
